raw: CHAPTER XV. The Footsteps Die Out For Ever
en: [Chapter 15] The Footsteps Die Out For Ever

raw: Along the Paris streets, the death-carts rumble, hollow and harsh.
en: Along the streets of Paris, the death carts rumbled, hollow and harsh.

raw: Six tumbrils carry the day’s wine to La Guillotine.
en: Six carts carried that day's victims to the Guillotine.

raw: All the devouring and insatiate Monsters imagined since imagination could record itself, are fused in the one realisation, Guillotine.
en: All the greedy and hungry monsters ever imagined throughout history were combined into this one reality: the Guillotine.

raw: And yet there is not in France, with its rich variety of soil and climate, a blade, a leaf, a root, a sprig, a peppercorn, which will grow to maturity under conditions more certain than those that have produced this horror.
en: And yet, in all of France, with its rich variety of soil and weather, there was not a single leaf, root, or plant that grew under conditions more certain than those that had produced this horror.

raw: Crush humanity out of shape once more, under similar hammers, and it will twist itself into the same tortured forms.
en: If you crush humanity out of shape again under the same heavy hammers of abuse, it will twist itself into the same tortured shapes.

raw: Sow the same seed of rapacious license and oppression over again, and it will surely yield the same fruit according to its kind.
en: If you sow the same seeds of greedy lawlessness and oppression again, it will surely yield the same bitter fruit.

raw: Six tumbrils roll along the streets.
en: Six death carts rolled down the streets.

raw: Change these back again to what they were, thou powerful enchanter, Time, and they shall be seen to be the carriages of absolute monarchs, the equipages of feudal nobles, the toilettes of flaring Jezebels, the churches that are not my father’s house but dens of thieves, the huts of millions of starving peasants!
en: Turn them back to what they used to be, powerful magician Time, and they would be seen as the carriages of absolute kings, the coaches of feudal lords, the dressing tables of greedy women, the churches turned into dens of thieves instead of houses of God, and the shacks of millions of starving peasants!

raw: No; the great magician who majestically works out the appointed order of the Creator, never reverses his transformations. “If thou be changed into this shape by the will of God,” say the seers to the enchanted, in the wise Arabian stories, “then remain so!
en: But the great magician Time, who carries out the Creator's plan, never reverses his transformations. “If you have been changed into this shape by the will of God,” say the wise men to the cursed in the old Arabian stories, “then stay that way!

raw: But, if thou wear this form through mere passing conjuration, then resume thy former aspect!”  Changeless and hopeless, the tumbrils roll along.
en: But if you wear this form because of a passing magic spell, then return to your old self!” Changeless and hopeless, the death carts rolled along.

raw: As the sombre wheels of the six carts go round, they seem to plough up a long crooked furrow among the populace in the streets.
en: As the dark wheels of the six carts turned, they seemed to plow a long, crooked path through the crowds in the streets.

raw: Ridges of faces are thrown to this side and to that, and the ploughs go steadily onward.
en: Waves of faces were pushed to this side and that, and the plows moved steadily forward.

raw: So used are the regular inhabitants of the houses to the spectacle, that in many windows there are no people, and in some the occupation of the hands is not so much as suspended, while the eyes survey the faces in the tumbrils.
en: The local residents were so used to this sight that many windows were empty, and in others, people did not even stop their work while they watched the faces in the carts.

raw: Here and there, the inmate has visitors to see the sight; then he points his finger, with something of the complacency of a curator or authorised exponent, to this cart and to this, and seems to tell who sat here yesterday, and who there the day before.
en: Here and there, a resident had guests over to watch the show; he would point his finger like a tour guide or museum guide, pointing out this cart and that, explaining who had sat there yesterday and who had been there the day before.

raw: Of the riders in the tumbrils, some observe these things, and all things on their last roadside, with an impassive stare; others, with a lingering interest in the ways of life and men.
en: Of the people riding in the carts, some watched the crowds and the roadside with a blank stare, while others showed a final interest in the ways of life and humanity.

raw: Some, seated with drooping heads, are sunk in silent despair; again, there are some so heedful of their looks that they cast upon the multitude such glances as they have seen in theatres, and in pictures.
en: Some sat with slumped heads, lost in silent despair; others were so concerned with how they looked that they cast dramatic glances at the crowd, like actors in theaters or portraits.

raw: Several close their eyes, and think, or try to get their straying thoughts together.
en: Several closed their eyes and thought, trying to collect their wandering thoughts.

raw: Only one, and he a miserable creature, of a crazed aspect, is so shattered and made drunk by horror, that he sings, and tries to dance.
en: Only one, a miserable man who looked insane, was so broken and crazed by horror that he sang and tried to dance.

raw: Not one of the whole number appeals by look or gesture, to the pity of the people.
en: Not a single person among them begged for the crowd's pity by look or gesture.

raw: There is a guard of sundry horsemen riding abreast of the tumbrils, and faces are often turned up to some of them, and they are asked some question.
en: A guard of several horsemen rode alongside the carts, and people in the crowd often looked up to ask them questions.

raw: It would seem to be always the same question, for, it is always followed by a press of people towards the third cart.
en: It seemed to be always the same question, because it was always followed by a rush of people toward the third cart.

raw: The horsemen abreast of that cart, frequently point out one man in it with their swords.
en: The horsemen next to that cart frequently pointed out one man inside with their swords.

raw: The leading curiosity is, to know which is he; he stands at the back of the tumbril with his head bent down, to converse with a mere girl who sits on the side of the cart, and holds his hand.
en: The crowd's main curiosity was to see which one he was; he stood at the back of the cart with his head bent down, talking to a young girl who sat on the edge of the cart and held his hand.

raw: He has no curiosity or care for the scene about him, and always speaks to the girl.
en: He showed no curiosity or interest in the scene around him, keeping his focus entirely on the girl.

raw: Here and there in the long street of St. Honore, cries are raised against him.
en: Here and there along the long Street of Saint-Honoré, people shouted curses at him.

raw: If they move him at all, it is only to a quiet smile, as he shakes his hair a little more loosely about his face.
en: If they affected him at all, it was only to bring a quiet smile to his face, as he shook his hair a little looser.

raw: He cannot easily touch his face, his arms being bound.
en: He could not easily touch his face, as his arms were tied.

raw: On the steps of a church, awaiting the coming-up of the tumbrils, stands the Spy and prison-sheep.
en: On the steps of a church, waiting for the carts to arrive, stood Barsad the spy, the prison sheep.

raw: He looks into the first of them: not there.
en: He looked into the first cart: Darnay was not there.

raw: He looks into the second: not there.
en: He looked into the second: not there.

raw: He already asks himself, “Has he sacrificed me?” when his face clears, as he looks into the third.
en: He was just starting to ask himself, “Did he betray me?” when his face cleared as he looked into the third cart.

raw: “Which is Evrémonde?” says a man behind him.
en: “Which one is Evrémonde?” asked a man behind him.

raw: “That.
en: “That one.

raw: At the back there.”
en: At the back there.”

raw: “With his hand in the girl’s?”
en: “With his hand in the girl's?”

raw: “Yes.”
en: “Yes.”

raw: The man cries, “Down, Evrémonde!
en: The man shouted, “Down with Evrémonde!

raw: To the Guillotine all aristocrats!
en: To the Guillotine with all aristocrats!

raw: Down, Evrémonde!”
en: Down with Evrémonde!”

raw: “Hush, hush!” the Spy entreats him, timidly.
en: “Shh, quiet!” the spy begged him nervously.

raw: “And why not, citizen?”
en: “And why not, citizen?”

raw: “He is going to pay the forfeit: it will be paid in five minutes more.
en: “He is going to pay his price; it will be paid in five minutes.

raw: Let him be at peace.”
en: Let him be in peace.”

raw: But the man continuing to exclaim, “Down, Evrémonde!” the face of Evrémonde is for a moment turned towards him.
en: But the man kept shouting, “Down with Evrémonde!” and the face of the prisoner turned toward him for a second.

raw: Evrémonde then sees the Spy, and looks attentively at him, and goes his way.
en: Carton saw the spy, looked closely at him, and then went on his way.

raw: The clocks are on the stroke of three, and the furrow ploughed among the populace is turning round, to come on into the place of execution, and end.
en: The clocks were striking three, and the path plowed through the crowd turned into the execution square, coming to an end.

raw: The ridges thrown to this side and to that, now crumble in and close behind the last plough as it passes on, for all are following to the Guillotine.
en: The crowds that had been pushed aside now closed in behind the last cart as it passed, for everyone was following them to the Guillotine.

raw: In front of it, seated in chairs, as in a garden of public diversion, are a number of women, busily knitting.
en: In front of the stage, sitting in chairs as if they were in a park for entertainment, were a group of women, busy with their knitting.

raw: On one of the fore-most chairs, stands The Vengeance, looking about for her friend.
en: Standing on one of the front chairs was The Vengeance, looking around for her friend.

raw: “Thérèse!” she cries, in her shrill tones. “Who has seen her?
en: “Thérèse!” she cried in her shrill voice. “Who has seen her?

raw: Thérèse Defarge!”
en: Thérèse Defarge!”

raw: “She never missed before,” says a knitting-woman of the sisterhood.
en: “She has never missed it before,” said one of the knitting women.

raw: “No; nor will she miss now,” cries The Vengeance, petulantly. “Thérèse.”
en: “No, and she won't miss it now,” cried The Vengeance crossly. “Thérèse!”

raw: “Louder,” the woman recommends.
en: “Shout louder,” the woman suggested.

raw: Ay!
en: Yes!

raw: Louder, Vengeance, much louder, and still she will scarcely hear thee.
en: Shout louder, Vengeance, much louder, and still she will barely hear you.

raw: Louder yet, Vengeance, with a little oath or so added, and yet it will hardly bring her.
en: Louder yet, Vengeance, with a curse or two added, and still it will not bring her.

raw: Send other women up and down to seek her, lingering somewhere; and yet, although the messengers have done dread deeds, it is questionable whether of their own wills they will go far enough to find her!
en: Send other women up and down to look for her, thinking she is lingering somewhere; and yet, even though these messengers have done terrifying deeds, it is doubtful if they would dare go far enough to find where she lies!

raw: “Bad Fortune!” cries The Vengeance, stamping her foot in the chair, “and here are the tumbrils!
en: “Bad luck!” cried The Vengeance, stamping her foot on the chair. “And here are the carts!

raw: And Evrémonde will be despatched in a wink, and she not here!
en: Evrémonde will be executed in a second, and she isn't here!

raw: See her knitting in my hand, and her empty chair ready for her.
en: Look at her knitting in my hand, and her empty chair waiting for her.

raw: I cry with vexation and disappointment!”
en: I could cry with anger and disappointment!”

raw: As The Vengeance descends from her elevation to do it, the tumbrils begin to discharge their loads.
en: As The Vengeance got down from the chair, the carts began to empty their passengers.

raw: The ministers of Sainte Guillotine are robed and ready.
en: The executioners of Saint Guillotine were ready.

raw: Crash!--A head is held up, and the knitting-women who scarcely lifted their eyes to look at it a moment ago when it could think and speak, count One.
en: Crash!, A head was held up, and the knitting women, who barely looked up at the person who could think and speak just a moment ago, counted One.

raw: The second tumbril empties and moves on; the third comes up.
en: The second cart emptied and moved on; the third pulled up.

raw: Crash!--And the knitting-women, never faltering or pausing in their Work, count Two.
en: Crash!, And the knitting women, never slowing down or pausing in their work, counted Two.

raw: The supposed Evrémonde descends, and the seamstress is lifted out next after him.
en: The man they thought was Evrémonde stepped down, and the seamstress was helped out right after him.

raw: He has not relinquished her patient hand in getting out, but still holds it as he promised.
en: He had not let go of her patient hand, holding it just as he had promised.

raw: He gently places her with her back to the crashing engine that constantly whirrs up and falls, and she looks into his face and thanks him.
en: He gently stood her with her back to the crashing blade that kept sliding up and falling, and she looked into his face and thanked him.

raw: “But for you, dear stranger, I should not be so composed, for I am naturally a poor little thing, faint of heart; nor should I have been able to raise my thoughts to Him who was put to death, that we might have hope and comfort here to-day.
en: “If it weren't for you, dear stranger, I would not be so calm, for I am naturally a poor, weak thing, faint of heart. I wouldn't have been able to lift my thoughts to God, who died so that we might have hope and comfort here today.

raw: I think you were sent to me by Heaven.”
en: I believe you were sent to me by Heaven.”

raw: “Or you to me,” says Sydney Carton. “Keep your eyes upon me, dear child, and mind no other object.”
en: “Or you to me,” said Sydney Carton. “Keep your eyes on me, dear child, and look at nothing else.”

raw: “I mind nothing while I hold your hand.
en: “I don't care about anything while I hold your hand.

raw: I shall mind nothing when I let it go, if they are rapid.”
en: I won't care about anything when I let it go, if they are quick.”

raw: “They will be rapid.
en: “They will be quick.

raw: Fear not!”
en: Do not fear!”

raw: The two stand in the fast-thinning throng of victims, but they speak as if they were alone.
en: The two stood in the quickly shrinking crowd of victims, but they spoke as if they were completely alone.

raw: Eye to eye, voice to voice, hand to hand, heart to heart, these two children of the Universal Mother, else so wide apart and differing, have come together on the dark highway, to repair home together, and to rest in her bosom.
en: Eye-to-eye, voice-to-voice, hand-in-hand, heart-to-heart, these two children of God, who were otherwise so different and lived such separate lives, had met on this dark path to go home together and rest.

raw: “Brave and generous friend, will you let me ask you one last question?
en: “Brave and generous friend, will you let me ask you one last question?

raw: I am very ignorant, and it troubles me--just a little.”
en: I am very uneducated, and it worries me, just a little.”

raw: “Tell me what it is.”
en: “Tell me what it is.”

raw: “I have a cousin, an only relative and an orphan, like myself, whom I love very dearly.
en: “I have a cousin, my only relative, who is an orphan like me, and I love her very dearly.

raw: She is five years younger than I, and she lives in a farmer’s house in the south country.
en: She is five years younger than I am, and she lives at a farm in the south.

raw: Poverty parted us, and she knows nothing of my fate--for I cannot write--and if I could, how should I tell her!
en: Poverty separated us, and she knows nothing of my fate, because I cannot write, and even if I could, how could I tell her!

raw: It is better as it is.”
en: It is better this way.”

raw: “Yes, yes: better as it is.”
en: “Yes, yes; it is better this way.”

raw: “What I have been thinking as we came along, and what I am still thinking now, as I look into your kind strong face which gives me so much support, is this:--If the Republic really does good to the poor, and they come to be less hungry, and in all ways to suffer less, she may live a long time: she may even live to be old.”
en: “What I was thinking as we rode along, and what I am still thinking now as I look into your kind, strong face which gives me so much comfort, is this: if the Republic really does good for the poor, and they become less hungry and suffer less, she might live a long time. She might even live to be old.”

raw: “What then, my gentle sister?”
en: “What then, my gentle sister?”

raw: “Do you think:” the uncomplaining eyes in which there is so much endurance, fill with tears, and the lips part a little more and tremble: “that it will seem long to me, while I wait for her in the better land where I trust both you and I will be mercifully sheltered?”
en: “Do you think,” her patient eyes, which showed so much strength, filled with tears, and her lips trembled slightly, “that it will seem like a long time to me while I wait for her in heaven, where I trust both you and I will find mercy and peace?”

raw: “It cannot be, my child; there is no Time there, and no trouble there.”
en: “It cannot feel long, my child. There is no time there, and no trouble there.”

raw: “You comfort me so much!
en: “You comfort me so much!

raw: I am so ignorant.
en: I am so uneducated.

raw: Am I to kiss you now?
en: Should I kiss you now?

raw: Is the moment come?”
en: Is the moment here?”

raw: “Yes.”
en: “Yes.”

raw: She kisses his lips; he kisses hers; they solemnly bless each other.
en: She kissed his lips, and he kissed hers; they solemnly blessed each other.

raw: The spare hand does not tremble as he releases it; nothing worse than a sweet, bright constancy is in the patient face.
en: Her thin hand did not shake when he let go of it; there was nothing but a sweet, bright courage on her patient face.

raw: She goes next before him--is gone; the knitting-women count Twenty-Two.
en: She went onto the scaffold before him, and was gone. The knitting women counted Twenty-Two.

raw: “I am the Resurrection and the Life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.”
en: “I am the resurrection and the life, says the Lord. He who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live; and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die.”

raw: The murmuring of many voices, the upturning of many faces, the pressing on of many footsteps in the outskirts of the crowd, so that it swells forward in a mass, like one great heave of water, all flashes away.
en: The murmur of many voices, the looking up of many faces, the pushing of many feet at the edge of the crowd, swelling forward like a great wave of water, all vanished.

raw: Twenty-Three.
en: Twenty-Three.

raw: ***** They said of him, about the city that night, that it was the peacefullest man’s face ever beheld there.
en: They said of him in the city that night that his was the most peaceful face ever seen there.

raw: Many added that he looked sublime and prophetic.
en: Many added that he looked noble and like a prophet.

raw: One of the most remarkable sufferers by the same axe--a woman--had asked at the foot of the same scaffold, not long before, to be allowed to write down the thoughts that were inspiring her.
en: One of the most famous victims of the Guillotine, a woman, had asked at the foot of the same platform not long before to be allowed to write down the thoughts that inspired her.

raw: If he had given any utterance to his, and they were prophetic, they would have been these:
en: If Carton had spoken his thoughts aloud, and if they were prophetic, they would have been these:

raw: “I see Barsad, and Cly, Defarge, The Vengeance, the Juryman, the Judge, long ranks of the new oppressors who have risen on the destruction of the old, perishing by this retributive instrument, before it shall cease out of its present use.
en: “I see Barsad, Cly, Defarge, The Vengeance, the juror, and the judge, along with long lines of the new oppressors who have taken the place of the old ones, dying by this same machine of justice before it stops being used.

raw: I see a beautiful city and a brilliant people rising from this abyss, and, in their struggles to be truly free, in their triumphs and defeats, through long years to come, I see the evil of this time and of the previous time of which this is the natural birth, gradually making expiation for itself and wearing out.
en: I see a beautiful city and a brilliant nation rising from this dark pit. Through long years of struggles to be truly free, in their victories and defeats, I see the evil of this time and the past time that caused it gradually paying for itself and fading away.

raw: “I see the lives for which I lay down my life, peaceful, useful, prosperous and happy, in that England which I shall see no more.
en: “I see the lives for which I give my own life, peaceful, useful, prosperous, and happy in that England which I will never see again.

raw: I see Her with a child upon her bosom, who bears my name.
en: I see Lucie with a baby on her chest who carries my name.

raw: I see her father, aged and bent, but otherwise restored, and faithful to all men in his healing office, and at peace.
en: I see her father, old and bent but with his mind restored, peacefully working as a faithful doctor to heal others.

raw: I see the good old man, so long their friend, in ten years’ time enriching them with all he has, and passing tranquilly to his reward.
en: I see the good old man, who was their friend for so long, passing away peacefully in ten years' time and leaving everything he owns to them.

raw: “I see that I hold a sanctuary in their hearts, and in the hearts of their descendants, generations hence.
en: “I see that I hold a sacred place in their hearts, and in the hearts of their descendants for generations to come.

raw: I see her, an old woman, weeping for me on the anniversary of this day.
en: I see Lucie as an old woman, crying for me on the anniversary of this day.

raw: I see her and her husband, their course done, lying side by side in their last earthly bed, and I know that each was not more honoured and held sacred in the other’s soul, than I was in the souls of both.
en: I see her and her husband, their lives completed, lying side-by-side in their graves, and I know that they honored each other no more than they honored and loved me in their souls.

raw: “I see that child who lay upon her bosom and who bore my name, a man winning his way up in that path of life which once was mine.
en: “I see that child who lay on her chest and carried my name growing up to be a man, succeeding in the same legal career that was once mine.

raw: I see him winning it so well, that my name is made illustrious there by the light of his.
en: I see him doing so well that my name is made famous and respected by his achievements.

raw: I see the blots I threw upon it, faded away.
en: I see the mistakes and stains I threw on my name fade away.

raw: I see him, fore-most of just judges and honoured men, bringing a boy of my name, with a forehead that I know and golden hair, to this place--then fair to look upon, with not a trace of this day’s disfigurement--and I hear him tell the child my story, with a tender and a faltering voice.
en: I see him, as a respected judge, bringing a boy who carries my name, a boy with a forehead I recognize and golden hair, to this very spot, which will then be beautiful and clean, with no trace of today's horror. And I hear him tell the child my story in a gentle, emotional voice.

raw: “It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known.”
en: “It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known.”
